questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was very inspired by the courses the University of Iceland offered. Especially the aspects of Ethics of Nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I definitely had an amazing stay in Iceland. I especially enjoyed the courses and the beautiful nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty good.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were given mentor groups, where we met some of the other students and had an Icelandic person as our mentor to tell us about Iceland and give us recommendations in general.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I felt safe and knew who to contact if I had any questions.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in student housing on campus. It was called Studentargarder, where we lived with other students. I had my own room and bathroom.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I shared a large, well-equipped kitchen with other 10 students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: In general, I had a really good experience. Maybe a good piece of advice is to find a thrift shop at the beginning of your stay, in order to make your room a bit more personal.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was really nice living in Studentargarder.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it pretty easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found some courses at home that I applied for pre-approval for. When I first came to the university, I changed one of my courses and changed it on Ugla. Then I re-send a pre-approval to my home university.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I just went to the international office at the University of Iceland on campus, and asked them what to do.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just ask the international office at the campus. They where really helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied with the academic program. The level of education was pretty high and we had a lot to do. But because I mostly went to Iceland because of the courses, it fit me very well.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of the courses I had were both for BA and MA.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Common for the style of teaching at UCPH and the University of Iceland was that the students were orally active. But in UCPH I am used to the exams at the end of the semester, whereas in Iceland it was distributed throughout the semester. We had a lot of smaller assignments and reports that we had to hand in, which could be stressful. My best advice is to make a calendar for yourself, where you put in all the deadlines. This helped me organize my studies.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Ethics of Nature 
Project in Ethics of Nature 
Icelandic Nature and Cultural Legacy 
Pronouncing and Listening 
Speech and Expression

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Ethics of Nature. This course was so inspiring to me, and I really liked the way of teaching. The course provided philosophical perspectives on nature and the current climate crisis.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I used most of my money on trips on the weekends. This was definitely worth it, but I was surprised at how much money it was to rent a car, etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Alcohol in general was very very expensive. But actually coffee in cafes was not that expensive. In general, the groceries were also pretty expensive, but this did not surprise me that much. The bus and the fitness were also pretty cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university had a fitness that I used a lot. It was really cheap and they had yoga classes two times a week, that I attended. This was really nice because it was also very close to where I lived.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Mostly it was fitness, but I also attended dance classes at Háskóladansinn, which was really nice and cheap.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you have the possibility just sign up for something. For me, it was really nice to attend both yoga and dance classes, because it was a nice way to meet other people, but also just to get some movement during some of the dark months.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: In general, I really enjoyed the trips during the weekends. It was so nice to see other parts of Iceland, but also just to hang out with some of the other students at the student cellar (the beer is also pretty cheap there). But also just to relax, and enjoy Reykjavik. I also enjoyed the sea behind the student housing a lot and just went on long walks.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: For me, it was pretty easy. Icelandic culture is in most ways not that far from the culture I am from.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I met some Icelandic people at student housing (I shared a kitchen with one), but also I met Icelandic students at the dance lessons. But to be honest, I mostly spent time with other exchange students, because this was more accessible.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Iceland is of course a pretty expensive country. This meant that I did not go out that often. But it helped that we had the student cellar because if was more affordable. Also, I had two experiences, where I was going on trips that got canceled due to the weather conditions. This was a bit disappointing, but the weather just controls the activities in Iceland in another way than I am used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I definitely loved the swimming pools in Reykjavik. I bought a half-year card, which I used maybe 2-3 times a week throughout the year. This was amazing, and I miss it a lot.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. The country is pretty expensive. Personally, this meant that I did not go out as much as I would do at home (go to restaurants, bars, etc.). But I actually enjoyed this. I used most of my money on trips on the weekends, which was a great priority looking back. Iceland is so unique in nature, and I had great hikes when traveling in the weekends.  
2. Sign up for something! For me, it was really great to have some activities throughout the week that I had to go to. Thereby I met nice people, and also I was a nice way to get some everyday routine. 
3. Go to the pools! This was such a nice way to spend time with the other exchange students and a very unique way of being outside in all kinds of weather.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go on trips during the summer period, before it gets too late because of the weather conditions.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: A good mix of inspiring courses, and Icelandic nature. This is both in regard to the trips on the weekends, and also in regard to the walks I did in Reykjavik near the coast. I enjoyed the mountains and the green moss so much.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I found the way of teaching (with the many assignments) a bit stressful and in some periods I had a lot to do in my courses. Sometimes it was difficult to find the balance between school work and being on exchange in a foreign country and all the experiences and emotions that follows,

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend going to the University of Iceland as an exchange student. Iceland is such a unique country, and the level of teaching was definitely fulfilling in the humanistic field.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
